punchline: There's a hole in your vision right now, and your brain hides it so well you'll never catch it without a trick.
thirty_sec: Each of your eyes has a blind spot where the optic nerve leaves, a patch that detects no light. You never notice it because your brain fills it in using what's around it. Your eyes also jump several times a second, but you see a steady world anyway. Neuroscientist David Eagleman's point is that the brain builds what we experience. So when you feel sure you saw something, remember that some of it was your brain's guess.
question: Want me to show you a hole in your own vision? All it takes is a pen, one closed eye, and ten seconds.
